evidence.excerpt:
Deep research tasks require agents to navigate large knowledge spaces, synthe-
size evidence across many sources, and adapt their plans as intermediate findings
emerge. Directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based multi-agent systems are well suited
to this setting because they support parallel execution and isolate each sub-task
within a focused dependency context. Yet existing DAG-based agents typically
instantiate a task-level plan before execution and then repair the graph only after
failures or missing evidence are observed. ThisPlan-then-Patchstrategy is brittle
for deep research: the system commits most strongly when its evidence is weakest,
and later revisions often waste computation on branches that should not have been
planned in the first place. To address this brittleness, we proposeDAGent, a DAG-
based multi-agent framework that introducesEvaluate-then-Growincremental
planning.

evidence.excerpt:
Instead of committing to a full DAG upfront, an Orchestrator grows the
task graph one batch at a time, conditioning each new expansion on confidence and
uncertainty signals from completed nodes. To support long-horizon evidence use
without overloading each sub-task, DAGent maintains a hierarchical context layer
that propagates compact QueryDocs by default while preserving full execution
traces for on-demand recall. The cleanly recorded DAG topology in turn admits
structural RL signals that an outcome-only recipe cannot define; we instantiate this
withDAGRPO, a GRPO adaptation that injects topology-conditioned credit on
Executor rollouts and a structural compliance regularization on Orchestrator plans.
Across BrowseComp-Plus, GAIA, and xbench-DeepSearch, DAGent surpasses the
strongest open-source baseline by 5.3 / 5.8 / 2.0 points at the Qwen3-235B-A22B
scale, with the lead replicating

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports a blinded human agreement study on 150 sampled predictions across all three benchmarks, with aggregate Cohen's kappa of 0.95 and 97.3% raw agreement between the human-majority label and the LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pass@1 accuracy on the three benchmarks is scored by GPT-4o-mini with GPT-4.1 as a tie-breaker against ground-truth reference answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: DAGRPO training on BrowseComp-Plus optimizes against trajectory-level binary correctness from the same LLM judge combined with structural compliance penalties.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior task accuracy, improved execution efficiency over Plan-then-Patch paradigms, and additive gains from topology-aware RL credit assignment are directly aligned with and supported by the presented ablation tables and cost metrics.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Empirical validation spans three recognized benchmarks (BrowseComp-Plus, GAIA, xbench-DeepSearch) across multiple open-source backbone scales (Qwen3-8B/32B/235B, Seed-OSS-36B, GLM-4-32B, Nemotron-3-Nano) and frontier GPT-5. The evaluation features appropriate baselines (ReAct, Summary, Fold, Flash-Searcher, FlowSearch), seed variance reporting, and thorough ablations of planning paradigms and RL reward components.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript validates the LLM judge against blinded human expert annotations across 150 sampled task predictions spanning all three benchmarks, achieving an aggregate Cohen's kappa of 0.95 and 97.3% raw agreement.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pass@1 accuracy on test benchmarks is scored using the automated LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini / GPT-4.1) against ground-truth reference answers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: During DAGRPO training on BrowseComp-Plus, the policy is optimized against trajectory-level binary correctness scored by an automated LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini with GPT-4.1 tie-breaker) combined with structural plan compliance penalties.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations: reliance on text pre-processing for multi-modal tasks, dependence on external retrieval quality, the correlational nature of the reachability closure proxy, restriction to benchmarks with verifiable closed-form answers, and limiting RL training to Qwen3-8B with LoRA.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formalizing the batch-by-batch Orchestrator expansion, structured per-node QueryDoc outputs, on-demand InteractionTranscript recall, and the DAGRPO policy gradient formulation with role-separated normalization and answer-inclusive closure weighting.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents a clear, well-scoped contribution to agentic planning and reinforcement learning with strong experimental controls, thorough ablation studies, and transparent discussion of boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript introduces DAGent, a multi-agent deep research framework featuring Evaluate-then-Grow incremental DAG planning alongside a hierarchical context propagation layer, and DAGRPO, an RL adaptation adding topology-conditioned credit assignment and structural compliance regularization.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work presents a clear, well-scoped contribution to agentic planning and reinforcement learning with strong experimental controls, thorough ablation studies, and transparent discussion of boundaries.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations: reliance on text pre-processing for multi-modal tasks, dependence on external retrieval quality, the correlational nature of the reachability closure proxy, restriction to benchmarks with verifiable closed-form answers, and limiting RL training to Qwen3-8B with LoRA.
